title: Services / MirrorMe
description: Whether the screenshare relay carries streams and who watches them: streams, groups and members, membership enforcement, then the pod and its node. A panel without data names something that does not exist at the moment, such as no group, no stream or no kick. MirrorMe logs carries every log line.

links.tooltip: Start page: every host, service and signal at a glance

links.title: Gateway requests to screenshare
links.tooltip: Requests through the Gateways, with their clients

links.title: MirrorMe logs
links.tooltip: Every log line of the pod, per container

list.name: Argo CD syncs
list.expr: (sum by (name, phase) (increase(argocd_app_sync_total{dry_run="false",name!~".+-mr-[0-9]+"}[2m])) > 0 unless on (name) sum by (name) (increase(argocd_app_sync_total{dry_run="false"}[1h])) > 6) and on () vector($syncs) > 0

list.name: Host rebuilds
list.expr: (max by (host_name, revision) (sysconf_installed_commit_time_seconds) unless max by (host_name, revision) (sysconf_installed_commit_time_seconds offset 15m)) and on () vector($rebuilds) > 0

list.name: syncs
list.label: Argo CD syncs
list.description: Marks each Argo CD sync on the time series.

list.name: rebuilds
list.label: Host rebuilds
list.description: Marks each NixOS rebuild on the time series.

panels.description: Available against desired. One replica by design: the media legs use host ports, so a rollout recreates the pod.
Whether the metrics listeners of the relay and the group service answered their last scrape. A dark half of this dashboard follows one of them being down.
Relay paths carrying a track. A path that something connected to without a track yet stays out.
Members holding a live lease, across the selected groups.
Every connection that the relay holds, publish and read alike, across all of its listeners.
Container restarts over the selected range. A relay restart ends every stream.
Out of the pod's interface. The VPS pays for this leg.
Egress over ingress. One publisher with three viewers reads 3. An idle pod reads near 1 on housekeeping traffic.
Pod CPU against the limits of its containers together. The streams decide the cost, so the limit holds three of the node's four cores.
Working set against the limits of the containers together.
Closes that the relay would not carry out over the selected range. Each one leaves a member whose lease lapsed and who may still watch.
Token requests refused over the selected range. A run of them means someone holds a key that this deployment does not sign for.

panels.title: Egress by transport
panels.description: Which listener the bytes leave through. The TLS and cleartext listeners of one protocol add up under the transport name that the app uses.

panels.title: Connections by transport
panels.description: A viewer reconnecting on its own shows as a step down and back up.

panels.title: Egress per stream
panels.description: One line per publisher, times its viewers. A stream that nobody watches costs nothing here.

panels.title: SRT packets lost
panels.description: SRT carries the default publish leg and no proxy wraps it, so a bad uplink shows here before a viewer reports a stutter.

panels.title: Paths the relay carries
panels.description: The relay configures one wildcard path, so each path here has something connected. Readers counts who reads it, the audience outside the group service. A path under public/ needs no membership.

panels.title: Who is connected
panels.description: One row per member holding a live lease, with the name that the app stated. The relay logs a connection under a keyed digest of it, which never leaves the group.

panels.title: Groups, members and publishers
panels.description: A member count climbing while the group count holds means a group filling up. Both climbing means a second group.

panels.title: Media clients
panels.description: Addresses that opened a media leg on netcup-g12 over the selected range, from its firewall log. The log holds the first packet of each connection, so a long stream counts once. Select an address to follow it.

targets.expr: conn.event:=new host.name:netcup-g12 destination.service:in(srt, rtsps, rtmps, moq, webrtc) | stats by (source.address, source.network, geo.country_name, geo.city_name) count() connections, count_uniq(destination.service) transports, max(_time) last | math round(last / 1000000) as last | sort by (connections desc) | limit 100

panels.title: Web clients
panels.description: Clients of the HTTP legs through the Gateways, such as WebRTC and HLS viewers and the app's API calls.

targets.expr: _stream:{service.name="hubble"} edge.event:=response backend.service:=screenshare/screenshare | stats by (client.name, client.network, geo.country_name) count() requests, count() if (http.response.status_code:>=400) errors | sort by (requests desc) | limit 100

panels.title: Connections closed
panels.description: What enforcement takes off the relay, by the list that the kick went to. A sweep runs on every membership change and every read, so a flat line while members leave means that a sweep misses them.

panels.title: Lease churn
panels.description: Leases stated, released and lapsed. A release follows an app that closed. A lapse follows an app that stopped refreshing, after a crash or a dead network alike.
Per-protocol connection lists that a sweep could not read over the selected range. That sweep saw fewer connections than exist, with the same result as a refused kick.

panels.title: Pod ingress and egress
panels.description: Both legs on one axis, so the gap between them shows the fan-out. The kubelet counts bytes at the pod's interface without knowing the stream or the member. Each point averages 5 minutes.

panels.title: Interfaces of netcup-g12
panels.description: The node's own counters per interface and direction. eth0 carries the public address that clients reach, tailscale0 the tunnel to the cluster. Only here do media and cluster traffic separate.

panels.title: CPU against the pod's limits
panels.description: The pod's usage against the limits of its containers together. The kubelet reports no usage per container, so this reading cannot name the container that spends it. Each point averages 5 minutes.

panels.title: Memory against the pod's limits
panels.description: The kubelet evicts on the working set. RSS beside it shows what the processes hold.

panels.title: Warnings and errors
panels.description: Warning and error lines per interval from all four containers, Go tracebacks included.

targets.expr: k8s.namespace.name:=screenshare ("[ERROR]" or "[WARN]" or "panic:" or "fatal error:" or "ERR" or "WAR" or "\"level\":\"error\"" or "\"level\":\"warn\"") | stats by (k8s.container.name) count() lines

panels.title: Recent warnings and errors
panels.description: The lines behind the bars, newest first. MirrorMe logs carries the whole stream.

targets.expr: k8s.namespace.name:=screenshare ("[ERROR]" or "[WARN]" or "panic:" or "fatal error:" or "ERR" or "WAR" or "\"level\":\"error\"" or "\"level\":\"warn\"") | copy severity_text as level
